observations: Nothing on main read resume.schema.json before this change; the 241 schema lines PR #56 added were unenforced, and its guard passed {owner}/{repo} and :owner/:repo. Enforcement now reads the rule from the schema, so there is one place to edit.

Importing build.py from the new test wrote __pycache__ beside it - a tenth directory under fixtures/ - and the count-of-nine guard failed on the first full-suite run. The loader now suppresses bytecode. The guard was right and was not loosened.

The regenerated fixtures differ from the sealed set at e37fa3b in exactly two ways: static.repository is present, and every source is resolved. resume_decision, oracles and next_action are byte-for-byte what they were.

Review finding G1: the schema and its README still said 'sealed before any fixture existed' after this change amended the schema and regenerated fixtures against it - the surface DEC-025 recorded as a #56 defect. Both now carry a dated amendment sentence; the schema constant is 2.0.0 because a document valid under 1.0.0 is invalid under it.

Review finding B1/B2: the refusal pattern was lexical and accepted $OWNER, OWNER/REPO, [owner] and a different repository entirely, and nothing tied owner/name to remote. Two cross-field rules now live in build.py - remote ends in /owner/name; a URL-shaped source references /owner/name - because JSON Schema cannot express them; the schema's description names both so a reader of either file sees the whole rule set.

Review finding B3: the schema declared owner/name patterns, a closed key set and a source minLength that build.py did not read. schema_rules() now reads every identity rule the schema can express; the only duplication left is the two cross-field rules, which have no schema form.

Review finding C1: the 'rules are read from the schema' test compared the file to a read of the same file and passed with the pattern hard-coded. A new test points build.py at an altered schema copy and requires the verdict to move both ways; the hard-coded mutant now fails it.

Review finding C2: build() judged per fixture inside the write loop, so a violation in fixture 08 was preceded by writing fixture 01. It is now two passes - judge all, then write - and the write-refusal test breaks one fixture while changing another benignly. The per-fixture mutant fails it.
The schema diff is now 19 insertions and 5 deletions on the original hand-formatted text instead of a 236-line reformat, so a reviewer can see the five semantic nodes (G3).
decisions: Read the rules from the schema rather than restating them in code or adding a JSON Schema dependency: one source, enforced, stdlib-only.
Refuse in write mode too. A generator that writes what the schema refuses is the defect.

declared_non_coverage: Only the identity rules are enforced by build.py; the rest of resume.schema.json is still a declaration nothing in CI reads (NS-006 in NEXT_STEPS.md is the planned full validation). The nine fixtures were validated against the full schema by hand with jsonschema 4.26.0, 0 errors each.

The refusal pattern has known false positives on shell sources that contain <, > or {} (a pipeline, a jsonpath, a gh command that resolves {owner} from cwd); no committed fixture uses one, and a source that resolves only from a working directory is refused on purpose.
The regenerated fixtures have not been run against any agent; WP-024's result stands unchanged.
The remote pattern checks shape, not reachability; it refuses credentials in the authority but cannot see a token elsewhere.
